montecristo-dr--classic-series.description: A Dominican series from Altadis U.S.A. that wraps a select Dominican binder and Dominican filler in a select Connecticut Shade leaf. The smoke stays on the mellow, smooth side, with an easy draw and a creamy, quietly sweet balance that suits newcomers and daytime smoking alike.

sources.title: Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo Classic Series
Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo Classic

montecristo-dr--white-series.description: Made in the Dominican Republic as a companion to the original Montecristo, the White Series pairs a hand-selected Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper with a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan long filler. It smokes creamy and well rounded around neutral wood and light earth, with a touch of pepper showing mostly on the finish.

thirds.notes: Neutral wood and light earth with a creamy, oily texture and a faint peppery finish.
The wood-and-earth core holds steady while the body eases back noticeably.
The same core returns to a solid medium body as the burn slows near the end.

sources.title: Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo White Series
Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo White Series
Cigar Obsession – Montecristo White Series Toro review

montecristo-dr--platinum-series.description: A Dominican-made Montecristo with a Cubano-seed wrapper from Mexico's San Andrés valley over a Dominican binder and aged Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian long filler. It sits at the fuller end of the range, bold yet balanced, with a quiet sweetness and leather building slowly toward a long, lingering finish.

thirds.notes: Opens with subtle sweetness over a woody base, the draw loosening after the first minutes.
Leather joins the sweetness and the strength begins a slow climb.
Reaches full body and holds it to the end, leaving a long finish on the palate.

sources.title: Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo Platinum Series
Leaf Enthusiast – Montecristo Platinum review

montecristo-dr--nicaragua-series.description: Produced at A.J. Fernández's factory in Estelí, this Nicaraguan puro was the first core Montecristo line made with an outside collaborator. Under a veined, oily wrapper it shows cedar and a sweet floral note over muted earth, with pepper that builds steadily and a blend that comes together best in the final third.

thirds.notes: Woody cedar with slight sweetness and a grassy edge, and pepper strong on the nose.
Floral notes rise to match the wood while the pepper grows and the earth holds steady.
Earth comes forward against the cedar, a sweet floral thread stays underneath and the pepper peaks.

sources.title: Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo Nicaragua Series
Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo lines overview
Leaf Enthusiast – Montecristo Nicaragua Series review

montecristo-dr--epic.description: Handmade at Altadis U.S.A.'s Tabacalera de García by the Grupo de Maestros, Epic wraps an Ecuadorian Habano leaf around a Nicaraguan binder and aged 2007 Nicaraguan and Dominican long filler. A full smoke for experienced palates, it moves from pepper and earth through coffee and cream toward baker's spice and a hint of orange.

thirds.notes: Exotic pepper on tongue and nose, grass and earth on the draw and cream in the background.
Coffee builds and settles into a coffee-and-cream profile as the spice turns toward baker's spice.
Orange citrus appears beside baker's spice and coffee; the finish stays clean as strength reaches full.

sources.title: Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo Epic
Cigar Coop – Montecristo Epic Vintage 2007 review

montecristo-dr--epic-vintage-12.description: Introduced in 2021, this Epic is built around Dominican tobacco from the 2012 harvest, cured and fermented before the Grupo de Maestros blended it with Nicaraguan leaf under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Made at Tabacalera de García, it shows coffee, earth and a raisin-like sweetness early, then gives way to cocoa, leather and clove-like spice.

thirds.notes: Coffee bean and sweet tobacco lead, with earth, pepper and a raisin-and-cashew sweetness in support.
Earth steps up beside the coffee, woody tones grow and a little chocolate replaces some sweetness.
Sweetness fades as earth, cocoa and leather take over, with clove-like spice near the end.

sources.title: Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo Epic Vintage 12
Cigar Coop – Montecristo Epic Vintage 12 Blue Toro review
Cigar Dojo – Montecristo Epic Vintage 12 Toro review

montecristo-dr--espada.description: Released in 2014 as the first Montecristo made in Nicaragua and the brand's first work with the Plasencia family, Espada is a Nicaraguan puro of vintage Jalapa, Ometepe and Condega tobaccos blended by the Grupo de Maestros. It smokes rich and smooth, moving from earth, cedar and coffee toward a peppery, woody close.

thirds.notes: Earth and cedar with light cocoa, black coffee and a citrus tang over white pepper.
Cedar and coffee move forward with a faint floral note, pepper settling close behind.
Pepper builds alongside cedar and earth, coffee still present as the body edges up.

sources.title: Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo Espada
Leaf Enthusiast – Montecristo Espada review
Cigar Coop – Espada by Montecristo Guard review

montecristo-dr--espada-oscuro.description: The darkest Espada, rolled at the Plasencia family factory in Estelí with a near-black Nicaraguan Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Full in strength yet smooth, it layers nuts, wood and pepper over cocoa, coffee and a deep sweetness, and is best kept for after dinner with something sweet alongside.

thirds.notes: Nutty and woody after lighting, with black pepper, a malty sweetness and later a hint of citrus.
A bourbon-like sweetness arrives with bittersweet cocoa, walnut and strong coffee as the pepper grows.
Spice and dry wood take over, sweetness fades and bitter cocoa closes the smoke at an intense strength.

sources.title: Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo Espada Oscuro Guard
Cigar Dojo – Montecristo Espada Oscuro Guard review

montecristo-dr--espada-signature.description: A limited Espada developed by Rafael Nodal, the Grupo de Maestros and the Plasencia family from aged leaf in the Plasencia tobacco library, offered in a single 6 x 55 size named Valiente. A Jalapa Colorado Claro wrapper over Estelí tobaccos gives a balanced medium smoke of natural tobacco sweetness, earth, hay and gentle pepper.

thirds.notes: Pepper, earth and hay mingle before natural tobacco takes the lead, with red pepper on the retrohale.
The tobacco grows richer and clearly dominant while hay and pepper both gain ground.
Pepper becomes the main supporting note without overwhelming, as hay and earth recede.

sources.title: Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo Espada Signature Limited Edition
Cigar Coop – Espada by Montecristo Signature Valiente review

montecristo-dr--1935-anniversary-nicarag.description: Created by Altadis U.S.A. for the brand's 85th year, this soft-pressed Nicaraguan puro uses tobacco from A.J. Fernández's farms and rests a further two years after rolling, aiming to echo the 1935 Cuban original. It smokes creamy and fragrant, with cocoa, coffee and earth over red pepper and a sweet tobacco finish.

thirds.notes: Cocoa and coffee lead over earth, dark fruit and red pepper, with roasted nuts on the retrohale.
Chocolate and coffee take the front as the pepper grows and the smoke turns a little sweeter.
Coffee and chocolate carry the finish with touches of cedar, the pepper staying a steady companion.

Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo lines
Leaf Enthusiast – Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua review
Cigar Coop – Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Churchill review

montecristo-dr--1935-anniversary-edicion.description: One of the two finalist blends for the 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua, set aside to age and released in 2023. Box-pressed at Tabacalera A.J. Fernández, it pairs a twice-fermented Jalapa wrapper with an Ometepe Criollo binder and Estelí filler, and smokes smooth and balanced, with earth, cedar and citrus ahead of a gradually rising pepper.

thirds.notes: Earth and natural tobacco lead, with citrus, mixed pepper, baker's spice and cedar in the background.
Earth stays in front as cedar builds, and pepper rises after the midpoint.
Pepper joins earth at the front as the tobacco fades; the spice is clear but never harsh.

sources.title: Casa de Montecristo – Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Edición Diamante
Cigar Coop – Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Edición Diamante Toro review

montecristo-dr--montecristo-original.description: The Dominican expression of the Montecristo name, also known as Montecristo Yellow, made by Altadis U.S.A. with a Connecticut Shade wrapper over a Dominican binder and Dominican filler. Its silky golden leaf burns cleanly and gives a smooth, gently rich smoke with a soft aroma and a creamy finish, suited to a calm morning or an easy afternoon.

sources.title: Altadis U.S.A. – Montecristo Original
